newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha rallies as physical trading quickens.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha rallies as physical trading quickens.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices rallied sharply on Wednesday after crude held some of its gains and traders said they were increasingly looking at arbitrage opportunities to the U.S.
A 35,000 tonne Greek cargo was confirmed sold this week at $232-$233 a tonne, to be sent to Houston by the end of the month.
Traders said as many as two other cargoes, a Suez and an Alex, may also cross the Atlantic, but these were not confirmed and they questioned if the arbitrage window was fully open and profitable.
A 20,000 tonne Moroccan cargo was also believed sold on Wednesday basis Rotterdam at high quotes plus $3 or $4, traders said.
"I think the market is balanced and for a balanced market the crack is too high," said one trader.

He thought the naphtha to crude crack spread should fall about $5 to $45 a tonne, from $50 now and a high of $55 in early November, which was the strongest since May. The crack rose from about $39 on Oct 18.

The NWE market was generally seen as balanced with end users mostly satisfied and at least two and possibly three Russian cargoes of 5,000 to 10,000 tonnes expected by the end of the month, traders said.
Algeria's Skikda port was shut late Tuesday because of bad weather, a shipping agent said, and it was not known when it would reopen.
Weather Services Corp said winds should slow down on Thursday and Friday to 10-15 miles per hour and 5-10 mph, respectively, before picking up again at the weekend.
"If it is closed over the weekend that could have an effect...But if the winds calm down to load one or two cargoes, then that is enough to keep the heat off," the trader said.
Dec swaps jumped $4 to $224/$225 and Jan rose by the same amount to trade at $218/$219.
Cargoes were up $1 at $226 cif, where an Egyptian cargo traded yesterday.
